'''Joseph Diestel''' (January 27, 1943 – August 17, 2017) was an American [[mathematician]] and Professor of Mathematics at [[Kent State University]]. In addition to his contribution to [[functional analysis]], particularly [[Banach space]] theory and the theory of [[vector measure]]s, Diestel was known for a number of highly influential textbooks: in 1975 he published "Lecture Notes Geometry of Banach Spaces—Selected Topics";<ref>{{cite book|title=Geometry of Banach spaces—selected topics.|last1=Diestel|first1=Joseph|date=1975|publisher=Springer-Verlag, Berlin-New York}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|last1=Дистель|first1=Джозеф|title=Геометрия банаховых пространств|date=1980|publisher=Vishcha Shkola|location=Kiev}}</ref> in 1977, he published "Vector Measures"<ref>{{cite book|title=Vector measures|last1=Diestel|first1=Joseph|last2=Uhl|first2=J. Jerry|date=1977|publisher=American Mathematical Society}}</ref> with J. Jerry Uhl; in 1984, published "Sequences and series in Banach spaces"<ref>{{cite book|title=Sequences and series in Banach spaces|url=https://archive.org/details/sequencesseriesi0000dies|url-access=registration|last1=Diestel|first1=Joseph|date=1984|publisher=Springer-Verlag, New York|isbn=0-387-90859-5}}</ref> and in 1995 he published "Absolutely summing operators"<ref>{{cite book|title=Absolutely summing operators|last1=Diestel|first1=Joe|last2=Jarchow|first2=Hans|last3=Tonge|first3=Andrew|date=1995|publisher=Cambridge University Press|isbn=0-521-43168-9|edition=1st publ. 1995.|location=Cambridge}}</ref> with H. Jarchow and A. Tonge; as well as a number of other books.<ref>{{cite book|title=The metric theory of tensor products : Grothendieck's résumé revisited|last1=Diestel|first1=Joe|last2=Fourie|first2=Jan H|last3=Swart|first3=Johan|date=2008|publisher=American Mathematical Society|isbn=978-0-8218-4440-3|location=Providence, R.I.}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|title=The joys of Haar measure|last1=Diestel|first1=Joe|last2=Spalsbury|first2=Angela|date=2014|publisher=American Mathematical Society|isbn=978-1-4704-0935-7}}</ref>

Diestel received his Ph.D. degree in 1969 from [[Catholic University of America]] under [[Victor Michael Bogdan]]. He had 29 graduate students and over 46 mathematical descendants.<ref>{{cite web|title=Mathematics Genealogy Project|url=https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=7622|website=The Mathematics Genealogy Project}}</ref>
